ships.checker_verdict: PASS after one fix cycle. THREE independent checkers, none given a prior verdict, all on a DIFFERENT MODEL from the maker. PASS 1 primary, verbatim: "VERDICT: PARTIAL - matcher is correct (0/56,766 divergences, 46/46, 64/64, 14/14 e2e), secure (0 XSS, no proto-pollution), private (1 request, 0 cookies/storage), and premises are docs-accurate, but the page's absolute printed claim 'No input can make it hang' is false: a pasteable pattern/value pair produces a measured 5.6 s synchronous tab freeze because the linear-time Pike VM is still O(pattern x value) with no input-size guard." PASS 1 independent security adversary, verbatim: "VERDICT: FAIL - the freeze/hang objective produced multiple reproduced, measured defects (up to a full tab crash and multi-ten-second blocks well past the claimed 50ms ceiling), directly falsifying 'No input can make it hang,' while the XSS objective found nothing across an exhaustive, corpus-plus-hundreds-more sweep." It measured 7,755 ms on 5,000 files x 100 patterns (proven a true event-loop freeze: a screenshot 300 ms in timed out without returning a frame, and a 5 ms interval canary ticked 3 times where ~1,358 were due), 12,889 ms on 2,000-level nested YAML with no glob patterns at all, >90 s unfinished on '*?'x20000, and a TAB CRASH on a 20,000-level document. FIX CYCLE (one, as the contract allows): a work budget decremented by NFA states actually visited and checked inside the loop - unlike ship 002's failed static budget it measures work already done rather than predicting an exponential blow-up, so it cannot be satisfied and exceeded at once; out of budget yields CANNOT TELL, never a verdict. Plus encode-each-value-once, cached NFA scratch state, 1 MiB / 20k-line / 64-level parser limits, textLength checked before .value, clear-before-compute, 5,000-file and 4,096-char field caps, and the printed claim narrowed to what was actually proven. TARGETED RE-CHECK by a fresh adversary on the fix diff, verbatim: "VERDICT: PASS - every reported defect is fixed and neither the cached NFA scratch state nor the shared work budget produced any wrong verdict across ~69.5k RE2-differential and 6.1k bounded-vs-unbounded comparisons; the only residuals are two low-severity, sub-second UX/copy nuances." Before/after it measured: 7,755 ms -> 150 ms; 5,618 ms -> 188 ms; 9,675 ms -> 238 ms; >90 s -> 194 ms; 12.9 s / tab crash -> refused in 0 ms with no crash; 4,578 ms -> 0.9 ms. TWO RESIDUALS CARRIED, NOT FIXED (recorded rather than ground down - the contract allows one fix cycle, and changing code after the verdict would mean staging something unverified): (1) LOW stale-verdict-repaint - run() is synchronous so the clear() at its top is never painted before the compute, leaving the previous verdict as the last painted frame for up to ~0.67 s; DOM state is correct and a MutationObserver confirmed the old verdict is never re-inserted as current. (2) LOW copy-latency-scope - the copy's 'about a fifth of a second' is scoped to matching work and matches the measured ~0.23 s budget, but pattern compilation and YAML parsing sit outside the budget, so worst-case total latency is ~667 ms, roughly 3x what a reader may infer. VERIFIED SOUND across the round: 211,118 (pattern,value) pairs by the maker plus 56,766 and ~69,500 by two checkers against their OWN Go/RE2 builds of act, ZERO divergences in every set; 203,082 reuse comparisons proving the cached scratch state never changes an answer; 6,144 bounded-vs-unbounded comparisons proving the budget only ever declines, never flips a verdict; GitHub's published cheat sheet 46/46 and act's own corpus 64/64 run against the LIVE page; 5 GitHub filter premises re-verified against docs.github.com; ~870 XSS payloads across every field including the thrown-Error sink, 0 injections, 0 prototype pollution; no new RegExp on user input, sole innerHTML assignment is a static ''; every stated limit off-by-one correct and named in its refusal message; 1 external request (the cookieless Cloudflare beacon), 0 cookies, 0 storage. Live-URL unverified by this run (egress; no desktop bridge in a scheduled run) - and health.json does not exist because .github/workflows/ has not been added to the repo.

ships.one_liner: paste a CODEOWNERS file and the paths a pull request touches, get the rule that wins per file, who GitHub would request, and the lines it silently skips
ships.gap_source_url: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners — EVERGREEN lane, why-now waived; the permanent demand is GitHub's own counter-intuitive precedence rule ("Order is important; the last matching pattern takes the most precedence") plus three documented footguns (! negation, [ ] ranges and \# escaping all silently do nothing) and silent line-skipping on any syntax error. Occupant hunt 2026-08-04, named and all CLI/library-shaped: hmarr/codeowners (Go CLI+lib), mszostok/codeowners-validator, orsinium-labs/owners, topfreegames/codeowners-verifier, nmusolino/codeowners, multimediallc/codeowners-plus (a GitHub Action replacement engine). GitHub's own web UI flags syntax errors but does not simulate a changed-file list against the rules. No free signup-free web page occupies the slot. Structural edge: free vs install-a-toolchain, paste vs checkout, whole file-list vs one path, explains the precedence decision, and runs entirely client-side so a private ownership map never leaves the browser.
ships.borrowed_from: hmarr/codeowners (MIT, Copyright (c) 2020 Harry Marr), pinned at commit 11d3ff2659b769bcb43ddef81a6ab19d1205d9c2 — parse.go's rule/owner state machine and match.go's buildPatternRegex segment rules ported line-for-line. Execution deliberately NOT ported: hmarr is linear-time only because Go's regexp is RE2, and a verbatim JS port into a backtracking RegExp would have reintroduced ship 002's ReDoS. Semantics ported, execution replaced with the lib/nfa.js Pike VM.
ships.checker_verdict:
FAIL. Two independent checkers, neither given a prior verdict, both on a DIFFERENT MODEL from the maker. ONE fix cycle was spent, as the contract allows, and the targeted re-check on the fix diff FAILED. Not staged; must not be presented as verified.

ROUND 1, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: FAIL - reproducible violations found in claims 1 (trailing-newline off-by-one lets an exactly-at-limit 20,000-rule/5,000-path file be wrongly rejected), 2/3 (200x500 refused in 14/14 trials instead of answering in 435ms, and one 601ms measurement beat the 550ms ceiling), 4 (#result.innerHTML measured at 1,000,117 chars via a dangling-tag bug from an unchecked b.push() at index.html:1476), and 5 (a real composited frame shows a stale complete answer with no pending indicator while the boxes already hold new input), plus a serious PII leak (GitHub handle and repo name baked into the newly-added, publicly-served public/ledger.json)." Its output-bound diagnosis was exact: the buffer's invariant held at the string level (999,994 chars) but an unchecked append left dangling <td> tags, and the browser's own HTML5 error recovery inserted the closers on assignment, producing 1,000,117.

FIX CYCLE (one, as the contract allows): line cap changed to count NON-BLANK lines; every append made one COMPLETE row with closers and the truncation disclosure moved into a 2,048-character reserve the cap cannot consume; the answer invalidated synchronously on the input event rather than after the 120 ms debounce; the timing prose re-derived as a RANGE over 24 repeated trials instead of a single reading; the unreproducible 200x500 figure restated as machine-dependent with both machines' results given; the handle and raw file URL scrubbed from the served ledger.

ROUND 2 targeted re-check by a FRESH adversary on the fix diff, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: FAIL - fix #1's blank-line exclusion reopens an unmetered paths-preprocessing loop that pushes the page's own reported timing to 1309-1342ms (2x+ the claimed 641ms ceiling) on a fully door-legal input, and the stale-answer fix leaves a pre-existing `running`-guard race that can strand the page permanently on 'working...' with a self-contradictory idle flag." It confirmed the other four fixes hold under attack: the line cap is exact in both directions across trailing-newline, CRLF, bare-CR and interspersed-blank shapes and admits no extra rules or paths past the door; #result.innerHTML never exceeded 1,000,000 (largest achieved 994,680) with every drawn row carrying exactly three cells, the table always closed, the truncation disclosure always present, and later sections cleanly suppressed rather than orphaned; screencast frames go old-answer -> "working..." -> new-answer with no frame showing a stale complete answer beside new input; and the machine-dependence passage is not overclaiming.

WHY THIS STOPS HERE. The contract allows one fix cycle and a targeted re-check. The re-check FAILED, so this is reported as FAIL rather than ground toward a soft PASS. Both new defects are precise and small, and both have the same shape as the original root cause rather than being new territory - which is why they become a rebuild constraint rather than another patch.

VERIFIED SOUND ACROSS BOTH ROUNDS (what the rebuild inherits): 171/171 reference pairs, 13/13 GitHub-documented cases and 6/6 line-skipping cases, all driven against the LIVE page's inlined engine, in both rounds; ~55-66 XSS payload-positions across every user-derived field (pattern, owner, path, comment, skipped-line text) with 0 injections, 0 dialogs and 0 page errors in both rounds; ~25 adversarial throw-probes including prototype pollution, lone surrogates and deep escape chains with zero uncaught exceptions; build reproducibility byte-identical (lib/inline.js output == shipped index.html) in both rounds; 0 cookies, 0 localStorage, 0 sessionStorage, exactly 2 requests (the page and the cookieless beacon), no pasted content in any request; mobile 375px with zero horizontal overflow including 250-char owners and paths; empty, whitespace-only, rules-without-paths and paths-without-rules states all clean; summary counts verified against hand-computed ground truth across mixed valid/malformed/blank/comment inputs. Live-URL unverified by this run (egress); see health.json - which does not exist, because .github/workflows/ has not been added to the repo.

ships.residual_defect: ONE ROOT CAUSE, FOUR SYMPTOMS. The page validates AGGREGATE input (total characters) but never the DIMENSIONS that actually drive work, and it cannot meter the browser at all once JavaScript hands over. (a) A single owner TOKEN has no length cap - MAX_OWNERS_SHOWN caps the COUNT, not the length - so `** @` + 100,000 'a' against 1,000 paths blocks 23,701 ms. The fix-cycle-3 comment named 'an owner list has no length cap' and then bounded the wrong axis of its own invariant. (b) The path-list split + per-line trim runs to completion BEFORE the MAX_PATHS check: 499,999 one-character lines blocks 8,408.7 ms and only then prints an accurate refusal. (c) innerHTML parse, layout and paint are outside any JS budget by construction; 810.4 ms dispatch-to-paint measured at exactly the maximum the page's own copy advertises as safe. (d) The problems panel collects entries unmetered (627.3 ms). Plus a correctness divergence of the same family: the reference silently drops a line >= 65,536 bytes AND every rule after it (Go bufio.Scanner ErrTooLong, unchecked by ParseFile); this port keeps going and shows a confidently wrong owner.
rebuild_constraint_design: 1. VALIDATE EVERY DIMENSION AT THE DOOR, before any split, trim, parse or compile - and count without materialising: total chars (already), LINE COUNT of both boxes (scan for \n with an early bail, never split first), per-line length, per-owner-token length, per-pattern length (already). Refuse naming the real number. Zero work before validation is the invariant; metering work you should not have started is the mistake this ship made three times.

2. BOUND THE OUTPUT BY CONSTRUCTION, not by budget. A JS tick cannot interrupt innerHTML parsing, layout or paint, so the DOM must be small before it is handed over: cap rows / owners / losing rules (already done) AND cap total rendered HTML length, then MEASURE PAINT - dispatch-to-double-rAF - not just a JS canary. The two disagree, and the user experiences the paint.

3. REPLICATE THE REFERENCE'S LIMITS, NOT ONLY ITS SEMANTICS. Go's bufio.Scanner drops any line >= 65,536 bytes and silently abandons the rest of the file. Either replicate that exactly (and show it, since it is a spectacular footgun worth surfacing to a user) or refuse such a line outright. Do not quietly diverge.
4. RE-DERIVE THE TIMING NUMBER FROM MEASUREMENT at the page's own stated maximum, and only after 1-3 hold. Do not print a ceiling before the architecture can honour it.

5. START FROM lib/checks/codeowners-oracle.json - 171 pairs, 13 documented cases, the line-skipping set, the Go differential recipe and six rounds of regression notes. The matcher itself is heavily proven; do not rebuild it.
